prohibitedPayloads: message, stanza, stream, session, or account identifiers
access tokens, authorization codes, redirect URIs, or query strings

signals.interpretation: Complete revision set and count of Waddle server targets that produced at least one build-info scrape in each preceding 60-second interval in the exact job, environment, cluster, and namespace scope; the only returned revision must be the evidence commit and every sample must equal the intended replica count.
signals.limitations: A matching build-info history proves scrape continuity and deployment identity at 60-second resolution, not readiness or journey correctness.

signals.interpretation: Aggregate process-generation start marker across the exact deployment scope; with the build-info target count held exact, the value must remain constant from the one-hour pre-window through the frozen end.
signals.limitations: This rejects observed process or container replacements that could erase process-local counters. It is an aggregate continuity check, not an instance inventory, and cannot detect a pathological replacement that reproduces the same floating-point aggregate.

signals.interpretation: Current connection-registry entries across all replicas.
signals.limitations: A clustered resource can have both a physical-socket entry and a foreign-owner relay mirror, so this is not a connected-resource, unique-human, or active-member count.

signals.interpretation: Current production room-registry entries across all replicas, sampled every 15 seconds.
signals.limitations: Registry entries can briefly include sealed, dead, or otherwise stale actors until registry cleanup, and the gauge can lag by one sampling interval. This is operational inventory, not community engagement.

signals.interpretation: Age in seconds of the oldest successful production room-registry sample across the requested deployment scope; every sample must remain between zero and 60 seconds.
signals.limitations: This proves the gauge sampler is fresh, not that every registry entry represents a live room actor.

signals.interpretation: Completed SASL1 OAUTHBEARER and SCRAM-SHA-256 exchanges, separated into bounded terminal outcomes. An explicit SASL abort or an unfinished exchange superseded by a new RFC 6120 auth request records the old exchange as cancelled; the replacement records its own terminal outcome, so one replacement flow intentionally contributes two exchange outcomes.
signals.limitations: SASL clients that disconnect before a terminal response, RFC 7628 OAUTHBEARER challenge exchanges that do not reach a terminal handler outcome, malformed XML rejected before the SASL1 handler, and invalid-phase re-authentication rejected at the frame boundary are not authentication exchanges. XEP-0388 SASL2 PLAIN used by XEP-0397 instant resumption and browser OAuth callback success are excluded, so this is not the full authentication denominator.

signals.interpretation: One typed sender-pass DM archive attempt or one room archive storage attempt by terminal outcome; chain_invalid is a permanent room archive-chain invariant failure.
signals.limitations: Room attempts include server-authored room system messages and are not exclusively sender-side. Direct chain_invalid remains zero because the guarded invariants are room-specific. Committed includes idempotent retries that found an existing archive row. It proves durable presence, not recipient visibility or the full accepted-message denominator.

signals.interpretation: Successful and failed connection-registry outbound-channel enqueue operations; both drop outcomes must remain zero.
signals.limitations: Delivered means one registry hop accepted an outbound item, not that a client handled or displayed it. A clustered delivery can increment once for a relay-forwarder hop and again for the physical WebSocket hop, so this is neither a resource-delivery nor logical-message denominator.

signals.query: sum by (surface) (label_replace(increase(waddle_delivery_terminal_error_drop_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "terminal_error_drop", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_message_archive_chain_invalid_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "archive_chain_invalid", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_pending_delivery_aged_out_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "pending_aged_out", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_pending_delivery_unresolved_poison_pill_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "pending_poison_pill", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_sm_detached_unacked_evicted_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "detached_unacked_evicted", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_sm_promotion_dead_lettered_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "promotion_dead_lettered", "", "") or label_replace(increase(waddle_sm_unacked_evicted_total{{scope}}[1h]), "surface", "unacked_evicted", "", ""))
signals.interpretation: Known permanent-loss, archive-chain invariant, replay-gap, ambiguous-drop, and corruption outcomes; objective is zero.
signals.limitations: Zero does not prove every accepted message was delivered; it only covers the named failure surfaces.

signals.interpretation: XMPP push candidates and publication jobs through the server-side XEP-0357 boundary.
signals.limitations: Publication does not prove provider acceptance, device receipt, display, or click.

signals.query: Faro event chat.journey.auth and measurement chat.journey.auth.duration_ms grouped only by outcome
signals.interpretation: Browser session bootstrap terminal outcome and duration.
signals.limitations: No provider, account, transport, redirect, or identity dimension is collected. It is a page/session measure, not unique users.

signals.query: Faro measurement chat.xmpp.message.acked.latency_ms percentile grouped only by kind
signals.interpretation: Client send bookkeeping to XMPP acknowledgement latency.
signals.limitations: This is not send-to-visible latency; the timer begins after the WASM send returns.

signals.query: Faro event chat.xmpp.session.lifecycle grouped only by type
signals.interpretation: Successful session-ready outcomes split between fresh bind and XEP-0198 resume.
signals.limitations: A fresh bind can be either an initial connection or a resume fallback; a separate reconnect denominator is still required for the Gate 1 resume SLO.

signals.interpretation: Elapsed time from reconnecting status to the next online status.
signals.limitations: Terminal reconnect failures have no duration sample and require the status/error events for a denominator.
